en nationalpark.explanation: "En nationalpark" means "a national park". It is built from "national" (national) and "en park" (a park). To say a place is Denmark's first one, say: "Nationalpark Thy var Danmarks første nationalpark" (Nationalpark Thy was Denmark's first national park).

en natklub.explanation: "En natklub" means "a nightclub". It is built from "nat" (night) and "en klub" (a club). The same "nat" is in "en natkjole" (a nightgown).

en natlampe.explanation: "En natlampe" means "a bedside lamp". It is built from "nat" (night) and "en lampe" (a lamp). The same "nat" is in "en natkjole" (a nightgown).

en nattesøvn.explanation: "En nattesøvn" means "a night's sleep". To say you need a good night's sleep, put "god" (good) in front: "Jeg trænger til en god nattesøvn" (I need a good night's sleep).

en naturkatastrofe.explanation: "En naturkatastrofe" means "a natural disaster". It is built from "natur" (nature) and "en katastrofe" (a disaster). To say a place was hit by one, say: "Området blev ramt af en naturkatastrofe" (The area was hit by a natural disaster).

en naturvejleder.explanation: "En naturvejleder" means "a nature guide". It is built from "natur" (nature) and "en vejleder" (an adviser). To say you go on a walk led by one, say: "Vi går en tur med en naturvejleder" (We go for a walk with a nature guide).

en navle.explanation: "En navle" means "a navel". The same "navle" is the start of "en navlestreng" (an umbilical cord). Do not mix it up with "et nav" (a hub), the middle part of a wheel: "Hjulet har et nav" (The wheel has a hub).

en navngivning.explanation: "En navngivning" means "a naming". It comes from the verb "at navngive" (to name). To talk about naming a baby, say: "navngivningen af barnet" (the naming of the child).

en nederdel.explanation: "En nederdel" means "a skirt". It is built from "neder" (down) and "en del" (a part), so it literally means "a lower part".

en nedgang.explanation: "En nedgang" means "a decline". To say an amount went down, use "i" (in) after it: "en nedgang i priserne" (a decline in prices). When you talk about a way down to a lower place, it means "a way down": "Nedgangen til metroen er her" (The way down to the metro is here).

en nedskæring.explanation: "En nedskæring" means "a cutback". It comes from "at skære ned" (to cut back). To say cutbacks are carried out, use "at gennemføre" (to carry out): "Kommunen gennemfører nedskæringer på skolerne" (The municipality is carrying out cutbacks at the schools).

en negl.explanation: "En negl" means "a nail", as in the nail on a finger or toe. To talk about a nail you hit with a hammer, use "et søm" (a nail): "Jeg slår et søm i væggen" (I hammer a nail into the wall).

en neglesalon.explanation: "En neglesalon" means "a nail salon". It is built from "negle" (nails) and "en salon" (a salon). To say you are going there to get your nails done, say: "Jeg skal have lavet negle" (I am getting my nails done).

en nerve.explanation: "En nerve" means "a nerve". To say something annoys you, use "at gå én på nerverne" (to get on someone's nerves): "Støjen går mig på nerverne" (The noise gets on my nerves).

en nevø.explanation: "En nevø" means "a nephew". To say a niece instead, use "en niece" (a niece): "Min niece er fem år" (My niece is five years old).

en niece.explanation: "En niece" means "a niece". To say a nephew instead, use "en nevø" (a nephew): "Min nevø er syv år" (My nephew is seven years old).

en nisse.explanation: "En nisse" means "a Christmas elf". In Danish folklore, "nissen" is a small creature in a red cap who plays tricks if people do not treat him well. At Christmas, Danish children put out "risengrød" (rice porridge) for him.

en nordmand.explanation: "En nordmand" means "a Norwegian". It is built from "nord" (north) and "en mand" (a man). To name the country, use "Norge" (Norway): "Han kommer fra Norge" (He comes from Norway).

en norm.explanation: "En norm" means "a norm". To say something is the normal way to behave, use "normen" (the norm): "Det er normen, at man siger tak for mad" (It is the norm to say thanks for the food).

en note.explanation: "En note" means "a note". To say you write things down while someone speaks, use "at tage noter" (to take notes): "Jeg tager noter i timen" (I take notes in class).

en notesbog.explanation: "En notesbog" means "a notebook". It ends in "bog" (book), like "en ordbog" (a dictionary) and "en lærebog" (a textbook).

en novelle.explanation: "En novelle" means "a short story". To say someone has written one, say: "Hun har skrevet en novelle om sin barndom" (She has written a short story about her childhood). Do not mix it up with "en roman" (a novel), a long book: "Romanen har 400 sider" (The novel has 400 pages).

en nuance.explanation: "En nuance" means "a nuance". When you talk about color, it means "a shade": "en nuance af blå" (a shade of blue).

en nummerplade.explanation: "En nummerplade" means "a license plate". It is built from "nummer" (number) and "en plade" (a plate). "Plade" also means "record", as in "en vinylplade" (a vinyl record).

en nyhed.explanation: "En nyhed" means "a piece of news". To talk about one item of news, say: "Det er en dårlig nyhed" (That is bad news). To talk about the news on TV or radio, use "nyhederne" (the news): "Nyhederne begynder nu" (The news is starting now).
